newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE STOCKS MOVE AHEAD AS TRADE PICKS UP.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE STOCKS MOVE AHEAD AS TRADE PICKS UP.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares moved ahead in active trade on Tuesday with brokers saying buyers were beginning to come back into the market, focusing mainly on heavily-weighted counters.
The key industrial index rose 25.86 points to close at 10,173.27 and brokers said they expected the market to remain firm for the rest of the week.
"We are seeing some buyers coming back basically in the heavy-capitalised counters. I think we will see the market looking firm this week," one broker said.

Among the day's winners, bankers Barclays leapt 100 cents to 3,300 as did FMB to 4,400, clothing retailer Truworths rose 25 cents to 925, building firm Mash gained 20 cents to 250 while winery Afdis at 480 and multi-industrial conglomerate TZI at 960 each added 10 cents.

A handful of counters bucked the trend, notably newly-listed manufacturing and construction company Randalls which brokers said came under some pressure with speculative investors selling to free up funds for merchant banker NMB's issue which closes on Thursday.

Randalls lost seven cents to 138, plastics and construction investor IHL dropped 100 cents to 2,100 while pork processor Colcom , clothing and furniture retailer Tedco and finance house UDC each shed 10 cents to 440, 270 and 310 respectively.
Minings were marginally firmer but with little volume across the board as metal prices remained flat. Falgold added two cents to 70 and Wankie Colliery put on five cents to 505.
The mining index edged 2.55 points up to end at 971.89.
